positions.claim: Fixed harnesses buy reliability by suppressing variance, and that suppression imposes a hard ceiling on novelty because determinism and emergence pull in opposite directions.
A carefully built harness can become irrelevant within a month because the underlying model improves enough not to need the scaffolding.
The factory/fixed-harness method is the correct approach for fixed, complicated problems and the wrong approach for moving, complex ones.
Complex systems cannot be planned or analyzed; the correct method is to probe, sense, and respond.
Most failures in modern design and engineering come from miscategorizing a complex problem as a complicated one, not from poor execution.
The harness should be the output of the engineering process rather than its input, emerging from agent interaction in ways that cannot be specified in advance.
Agent identity, roles, and specialization should arise from position relative to other agents and environmental pressure rather than being assigned by the engineer.
Central authority in a multi-agent system leads to brittleness in a changing environment, so governance should emerge from local coordination.
Horizontal intelligence (coordination among agents) is a higher-leverage direction than vertical intelligence (making individual agents smarter, as in self-improving skill-learning agents).
Pi's extensibility counts as design-stage adaptivity, not adaptive engineering, because it is not a self-organizing multi-agent system that reorganizes during runtime.
The rate of coupling between agents is the engineer's primary new control lever in adaptive systems.
Adaptive engineering will produce monoculture unless agent diversity is engineered, because agents are trained on the same data.
Without a genuine selection pressure analogous to environmental pressure in evolution, emergent agent systems will drift or settle into suboptimal attractors.
The binding constraint on future AI engineering will be harness adaptability rather than model strength.
Legibility and explainability necessarily degrade as system adaptability increases, and this is an inherent feature of complex systems rather than a fixable defect.
Fixed and adaptive engineering lie on a continuum rather than being a binary choice, and neither is superior — they serve different use cases.
